title: WALTEUR Tool Guardrail Coverage
description: Runtime guardrail-coverage table for an AI/agent build: every agent-callable tool declares pre-call, post-call, and error-path guardrails. Composes on top of tool-contract.schema.json (which proves the static contract) by proving the runtime bands wired around each call and full coverage of every declared tool.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of this manifest shape.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the last update.

policy.description: One-line statement of the guardrail policy this manifest enforces.

no_external_tools.description: Explicit ack that this build invokes NO agent-callable tools. Required to be true for an empty `tools` table with no tool-contracts (gate rule G7) — an empty table no longer passes silently.

tools.description: One entry per agent-callable tool. Every declared tool-contract must appear here (coverage rule G6, enforced by tool-guardrail-gate.sh).

tool.description: Tool name. When tool-contracts exist, must match a declared contract name.

side_effect_class.description: Blast-radius class. Kept in lock-step with tool-contract.schema.json.

external.description: True when the tool reaches outside the process (network, payment rail, third-party API, filesystem outside the workspace). External or dangerous tools trigger the stricter invariant (G5).

checks.description: Validations run BEFORE invocation: arg schema-validation, authorization/oversight, quota/rate-limit, prompt-injection scrub of arguments.

evidence_ref.description: Path to the code or config that implements the pre-call guardrail.

checks.description: Validations run AFTER invocation on the tool RESULT before the model consumes it: result schema-validation, injected-instruction scrub, PII redaction, output size bound.

evidence_ref.description: Path to the code or config that implements the post-call guardrail.

retryable.description: Error classes safe to retry (may be empty).

fatal.description: Error classes that must NOT be silently retried (may be empty).

on_fatal.description: Action taken on a fatal error. A silent no-op ("continue", "ignore", "swallow", "none", "") is rejected by the gate; dangerous/external tools require a halting/recovering action (halt|escalate|rollback|compensate|abort|replan). `replan` routes the failed call back to the planner (Reject+Replan).

evidence_ref.description: Path to the code or config that implements the error-path handling.
